options: One endpoint, extends forever one way
questions.explanation: A ray starts at one endpoint and continues forever in one direction.
questions.misconception: The shape with two endpoints is a segment and the one with none is a line — a ray has exactly one endpoint.

questions.prompt: Which point comes first in 'ray AB'?
questions.explanation: The endpoint always comes first when naming a ray.
questions.misconception: Ray AB means starting at A and heading through B — the endpoint leads the name, so AB and BA name different rays.

questions.prompt: To draw a ray, you use...
questions.explanation: A ray shows its one end with a dot and its endless direction with one arrowhead.
questions.misconception: Two arrowheads would mean a line, and two dots would make it a segment — a ray needs exactly one of each.

questions.prompt: What do two rays sharing an endpoint form?
questions.explanation: Two rays from one shared endpoint make an angle; the shared point is the vertex.
questions.misconception: Only rays that share a start point form an angle — two separate rays are just two rays, and the sharing is essential.

questions.prompt: In the angle, the shared endpoint of the rays is called the...
questions.explanation: The common endpoint where two rays meet in an angle is the vertex.
questions.misconception: The vertex is the corner point of the angle; the arrowhead and midpoint are different features of other figures.
